description:
Fetch the full declension (nominals) or conjugation (verbs) table for a
lemma identified by a search result's inflection handle (entry_id +
word_class). Use this only when a search ran without inline forms or left a
match un-expanded — a default search already returns each match's table
inline. Returns Markdown plus the table as structuredContent with the shape
{"result": <paradigm>} per the declared outputSchema — switch on
result.category ('nominal' | 'verbal' | 'not_found') before reading the body.
Content from en.wiktionary.org (CC BY-SA 4.0).

entry_id.description: The Wiktionary page title (the lemma) from a search result's inflection handle, e.g. 'amo', 'aqua'.
entry_id.title: Entry Id

word_class.description: The part-of-speech section from a search result's inflection handle, e.g. 'verb', 'noun', 'adjective'.
word_class.title: Word Class

name: latin_get_inflections

LatinNominalParadigm.description:
Declension of a noun/adjective/etc.: case → {singular, plural}.

``category`` discriminates this from the verbal and not-found shapes — switch on
it before reading the body.

cases.description: Case name (lower-case: 'nominative', 'genitive', …) → its singular/plural forms, in table order.
cases.title: Cases

LatinVerbalParadigm.description:
Conjugation of a verb, grouped the way Wiktionary's table is:
finite cells keyed by "<voice> <mood> <tense>" → person/number → form, plus the
non-finite sections (infinitives, participles, gerund, supine).

finite.description: '<voice> <mood> <tense>' (lower-case, e.g. 'active indicative present') → person/number ('first singular' … 'third plural') → the form. Periphrastic rows (e.g. passive perfect) appear under the single key 'all'. Alternates are comma-separated; an em-dash cell (no such form) is omitted.
finite.title: Finite

nonfinite.description: Non-finite section ('infinitive', 'participle', 'gerund', 'supine') → label ('active present', 'genitive', …) → the form.
nonfinite.title: Nonfinite

NumberForms.description:
A declension cell: the two number forms of one case. Latin forms are verbatim
(macrons preserved); alternates stay space-separated as Wiktionary renders them.
NumberForms.title: NumberForms

ParadigmNotFound.description:

page doesn't exist). ``found`` is False and there is no table body.
